2019_136_061119spmtg.paragraph: Agenda and full board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education special meeting of June 11, 2019, held at 5:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The centerpiece is a public hearing on the proposed 2019-20 budget presented by Assistant Superintendent for Business Services Rick West, followed by a 2018-19 budget amendment and the 2019-20 appropriations resolution, which appropriates $158,261,349 in the General Fund against projected revenue of $157,288,640 and certifies millage of 18.0000 non-homestead, 4.8836 homestead hold-harmless, 4.1000 debt and 0.9857 sinking fund. Purchase and contract awards, a $507,182.50 science materials adoption and an administrative appointment complete the packet.

**Meeting**
Special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, June 11, 2019, 5:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices are at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000; meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition**
- Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence mini-grant recipients, introduced by TFEE President Julie McClure.
- Mission Moment: Larson Middle School's Plastic Ocean Project; teachers Sandy Bammel, Shannon Dziwanowski and Dave Ivanko named TFEE Innovators of the Year; introduced by Principal Joe Duda.
- Larson Middle School received the 2019 National School of Character Award from Character.org, one of only 88 schools nationwide.

**Public hearing: proposed 2019-20 budget (Rick West)**

| General Fund | Audited 6/30/2018 | Final Amendment 6/30/2019 | Recommended 6/30/2020 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Projected revenue | $151,774,253 | $154,394,746 | $157,288,640 |
| Projected expenditures | $150,737,172 | $155,576,715 | $158,261,349 |
| Revenue (under) expenditures | $1,037,081 | ($1,181,969) | ($972,709) |
| Beginning fund equity July 1 | $24,205,391 | $25,242,472 | $24,060,503 |
| Ending fund equity June 30 | $25,242,472 | $24,060,503 | $23,087,794 |
| Fund equity as % of expenditures | 16.75% | 15.47% | 14.59% |

Assumptions: blended enrollment of 13,050, a decrease of 46 students from 13,096; a projected foundation allowance of $9,295, a $100 per pupil increase; a $1.1 million transfer from the Adult Education and Community Service Fund; a net salary increase of 1.0%; the effective retirement rate rising from 26.18% to 27.50% and the MPSERS UAAL rate from 12.21% to 12.41%; FICA unchanged at 7.65%; purchased services up 2.3% and supplies up 5.9% for the science adoptions.

**Millage rates**

| Levy | 2018-19 | 2019-20 proposed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Homestead hold harmless | 5.2320 | 4.8836 |
| Non-homestead operating | 18.0000 | 18.0000 |
| Commercial personal property operating | n/a | 10.8836 |
| Debt retirement (all property) | 4.1000 | 4.1000 |
| Sinking fund (all property) | 0.9922 | 0.9857 |

West's May 31, 2019 memorandum to Dr. Rich Machesky reports taxable valuation from the Oakland County Equalization Department up $188,487,760, or 4.83%. The hold-harmless levy is authorized to generate $1,034.18 per student; estimated sinking fund revenue for 2019-20 is $4,033,588.

**Action items**

| Item | Amount / terms | Funding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bid Pack #23 resolution amendment | $5,818,684.50 | 2016 Capital Projects, Sinking and Food Service Funds |
| Middle school science materials (SEPUP kits) | $507,182.50 | 2019-20 school year |
| Niles Center roof replacement, Royal West | $179,300.00 incl. contingency | 2016 Capital Projects Fund |
| Telecommunications, TelNet Worldwide | 2019/20 through 2021/22 | SIP trunking contract |
| Monitors and lab hardware (Presidio; Logical Ram Solutions) | $103,619.00 | 2016 Capital Projects Fund |
| iPads (Apple) and cases (Rug-Ed) | $367,500.00 and $23,232.00 | 2016 Capital Projects and Preschool Funds |
| Preschool laptops/desktops, Presidio | $39,823.00 | Troy School District Preschool Fund |
| Transportation, First Student | three years, July 1, 2019-June 30, 2022 | contract extension |
| Tractor/loader, Rochester Lawn Equipment | $30,969.12 | 2016 Capital Projects Fund |

**Personnel and other**
Natalie Haezebrouck was recommended for a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure as Director of Teaching and Learning effective July 1, 2019. The meeting closed with Superintendent Dr. Rich Machesky introducing the "2018-2019 School Year in Review" video.
2019_136_061119spmtg.verbose:
**Meeting.** Special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, June 11, 2019, 5:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and posted at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition.** Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence mini-grant recipients were recognized, with TFEE President Julie McClure introducing them. The Mission Moment honored Larson Middle School's year-long 8th grade Plastic Ocean Project; teachers Sandy Bammel, Shannon Dziwanowski and Dave Ivanko were named TFEE Innovators of the Year, with Principal Joe Duda introducing students Audrey Brown, Stephen Carlier, Jordan Cruz, Jenna DeJonckheere, Allison Diebol and Gabby Leonard. Larson also received the 2019 National School of Character Award from Character.org, one of only 88 schools nationally.

**Budget hearing and fund structure.** Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, presented the preliminary 2019-20 budget and draft budget book, covering the General Fund (1xx), Debt Retirement Funds (3xx), Capital Projects Funds (414, 416, 419), Early Childhood Center Capital Projects Fund (418), Sinking Fund (498), Capital Maintenance Fund (499), Food Service Fund (520), TCC Grant Fund (529), Community Service Fund (530), Troy Preschool Fund (531, effective July 1, 2019), Facility Rental Fund (535) and Troy School and Student Activities Fund (570).

**Taxable value and millage.** Homestead taxable value is shown as $2,663,539,694 in 2018 and $2,761,994,935 in 2019; non-homestead $1,240,757,317 and $1,327,909,275; totals $3,904,297,011 and $4,089,904,210. West's May 31, 2019 memorandum to Superintendent Dr. Rich Machesky reports taxable valuation on all property up $188,487,760, or 4.83%, per the Oakland County Equalization Department. The hold-harmless millage, levied only on homestead property, is authorized to generate $1,034.18 per student and is proposed at 4.8836 mills, a decrease of .3484 mills from 5.2320. Non-homestead operating is 18.0000 mills; commercial personal property is levied at 10.8836 mills and industrial personal property at 4.8836 mills. Debt retirement remains 4.1000 mills; the sinking fund rate falls .0065 to .9857 mills, with estimated 2019-20 sinking revenue of $4,033,588. Proposed totals are 15.9693 homestead and 29.0857 non-homestead, against 16.3242 and 29.0922 in 2018-19. A note records that in 1993-94 all taxpayers paid 31.0674 mills for operating purposes, and that rates are finalized with the L-4029 under Truth in Taxation, MCL Section 211.24e.

**General Fund assumptions.** Blended enrollment is assumed at 13,050, down 46 from the 2018-19 blended count of 13,096; the spring 2019 count was 13,061.16, requiring a fall 2019 count of 13,048.76 under the 90%/10% formula. Enrollment history: 12,563, 12,717, 12,878, 13,081, 13,096 and 13,050. The foundation allowance is projected at $9,295, a $100 per pupil increase; the Governor's proposal would provide $180 per pupil and the Senate's $100, with the House proposal unknown. Foundation history: $8,885, $8,955, $9,015, $9,075, $9,195 and $9,295. Other financing sources include a $1.1 million transfer of excess fund balance from the Adult Education and Community Service Fund. Salaries assume a net 1.0% increase, roughly $773,000. The retirement rate rises from 38.39% to 39.91% effective October 1, 2019; the UAAL rate rises 0.20 basis points, or 1.6%, from 12.21% to 12.41%; the effective retirement rate rises 1.32 basis points, the equivalent of 5%, from 26.18% to 27.50%, offset by state "UAAL Rate Stabilization." FICA remains 7.65%; PA 152 health caps for 2020 equal 2019 limits increased 1.0%. Purchased services rise 2.3% (about $469,000) and supplies 5.9% (about $426,000). Listed budget opportunities: staffing, healthcare aides, substitute teachers, professional development, Performance Based Compensation, Pay to Participate and Schools of Choice.

**General Fund figures.** Audited 6/30/2018: revenue $151,774,253, expenditures $150,737,172, $1,037,081 surplus, ending fund equity $25,242,472 (16.75%). Final 6/30/2019 amendment: revenue $154,394,746, expenditures $155,576,715, ($1,181,969), ending equity $24,060,503 (15.47%). Recommended 6/30/2020: revenue $157,288,640, expenditures $158,261,349, ($972,709), ending equity $23,087,794 (14.59%). Revenue by source for 2019-20: local $40,561,662, state $103,282,321, federal $4,216,617, incoming transfers and other $9,228,040. Expenditures by object: salaries $77,189,826, benefits $50,286,826, purchased services $20,620,857, supplies $7,751,605, capital outlay $333,269, other $224,816, outgoing transfers $1,854,150. By function: basic programs $84,075,673 (elementary $35,163,550, middle school $19,518,132, high school $28,878,426), added needs $21,980,397 (special education $14,526,781, compensatory $6,673,785, career and technical $779,831), adult/continuing education $790,292, total instruction $106,846,362; support services $51,191,443, including pupil $10,924,985, instructional staff $9,124,866, school administration $8,499,351, operations and maintenance $10,776,242, pupil transportation $3,861,809 and central services $3,173,290; community services $223,544. The ten-year history runs from 2010-11 revenue of $137,351,597 and expenditures of $137,073,867 to projected 2019-20 revenue of $156,086,440, with the fund balance percentage moving from 14.4% in 2010-11 to a projected 14.6%.

**Other funds, 2019-20.** Food Service: revenues $3,455,890 (local $2,281,500, state $107,000, federal $1,067,390), expenditures $3,435,345, transfers out $20,000, ending balance $4,690. Troy Career Center: state $60,000, federal $2,385,150, expenditures $2,400,150 plus $45,000 transfers out, zero balance. Adult Education and Community Service: local $3,021,900, expenditures $1,952,976, transfers out $1,100,000, ending balance $544,954; by program, Continuing Education $630,000 and CARE Co. $2,391,900 in revenue. Facility Rentals: local $135,000, expenditures $161,780, ending balance $246,925. Troy School District Preschool: local $2,021,500, expenditures $1,996,615 including $233,615 debt service, ending balance $69,180. Troy School and Student Activities: $5,000,000 in and out, ending balance $2,000,000. Debt Service Funds: property taxes $16,210,086, investment earnings $45,000, state $192,514, total $16,447,600; principal $12,235,000, interest $5,503,110, other bond expenditures $2,500, total $17,740,610, ending balance $1,124,544. By fund, expenditures are $4,708,156 (2012 Fund 312), $3,878,000 (2014 Fund 314), $4,408,250 (2015 Fund 315), $2,672,140 (2016 Fund 316) and $2,074,064 (2019 Fund 319). The debt payment schedule through 2039-40 totals $146,700,000 principal and $42,178,225.89 interest, $188,878,225.89 combined. Capital funds: 2016 Capital Projects (Series II) capital outlay $8,832,462; Early Childhood Learning Center building and site improvements $6,068,633 plus furniture and equipment $1,071,300 with $5,232,000 sale of land; 2019 Capital Projects (Series III) capital outlay $5,000,000 leaving $22,168,593 after $26,998,655 of bond proceeds; Capital Maintenance purchased services $500,000 leaving $496,469; Sinking Fund revenue $4,030,000 and capital outlay $3,828,500, leaving $201,500. Grants described include At-Risk, Bilingual Education, CFE Millage, Early Literacy, Great Start Readiness, IDEA-Flowthrough, IDEA-Preschool, Titles I through IV and Workforce Investment Act funds tied to Oakland County Michigan Works!

**2018-19 budget amendment.** Amended appropriations: General Fund $155,576,715; Food Service $4,334,204; Adult Education and Community Service $3,816,201; Preschool $381,705; Facilities Rental $748,176; Capital Maintenance $190,000; 2014 Capital Projects $107,185; 2016 Capital Projects $15,320,000; 2019 Capital Projects $130,062; Early Childhood Learning Center Capital Projects $13,000,000; Sinking Fund $3,882,000; Debt Service $15,399,958. General Fund revenue moves from $153,199,134 to $154,394,746, a change of $1,195,612, and expenditures from $155,009,522 to $155,576,715, a change of $567,193, lifting projected June 30 fund balance from $23,432,084 to $24,060,503. State revenue rose $926,625; pupil support rose $293,757; pupil transportation fell $140,128; the Early Childhood Learning Center sale-of-land estimate dropped $3,283,000 to $372,413.

**2019-20 appropriations resolution.** General Fund $158,261,349; Food Service $3,455,345; Troy Career Center $2,445,150; Adult Education and Community Service $3,052,976; Preschool $1,996,615; Facilities Rental $161,780; Troy School and Student Activities $5,000,000; Capital Maintenance $500,000; 2016 Capital Projects $8,582,462; 2019 Capital Projects $5,000,000; Early Childhood Learning Center Capital Projects $5,232,000; Sinking Fund $3,828,500; Debt Service $17,740,610. Certified millage: non-homestead 18.0000, commercial personal property 10.8836, homestead 4.8836, debt retirement 4.1000, sinking fund 0.9857.

**Consent and curriculum.** The December 18, 2018 Bid Pack #23 resolution is amended so the $5,818,684.50 award is an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund, Sinking Fund and Food Service Fund. Awards covered Schroeder, Troy Union, Smith, International Academy East and Troy High and included BNE Masonry $349,100.00, Men of Steel $48,000.00, Advanced Building Group $394,319.00, JD Candler Roofing $20,310.00, Hewett Company $434,249.00, Continental Contracting $209,500.00, Seven Brothers Painting $49,584.00, Great Lakes Hotel Supply $266,495.00, CMS Mechanical $881,133.00, Contrast Mechanical $990,000.00, MCMI $598,050.00, Great Lakes Power & Lighting $767,000.00, Brencal Contracting $306,200.00 and contingency of $504,744.50, reviewed by TSD Operations, TMP Associates, Peter Basso & Associates and Barton Malow. Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity and Accountability, presented the grades 6-8 science adoption of SEPUP Science Kits at $507,182.50 following a June 4 special board workshop; piloted programs were SEPUP (Lab-Aids), IQWST (Activate Learning), HMH Science Dimensions, FOSS (Delta Education) and Cereal City Science, reviewed with a modified EQUIP rubric published by Achieve and aligned to NGSS on the district's seven-year adoption cycle.

**Business awards.** Niles Center roof replacement (Public Bid 9889) goes to Royal West Roofing at a base bid of $163,000.00, total request $179,300.00 including 10% contingency from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund; Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations, and WeatherTech Consulting Group (Peter Kinnunen) recommended it after a 5/14/19 pre-bid conference and two sealed bids opened 5/23/19, the other from Schena Roofing. Telecommunications go to TelNet Worldwide for 2019/2020, 2020/2021 and 2021/2022, replacing PRI circuits with SIP trunking; Beth Soggs, Director of Technology, and consultants Abilita evaluated eight bids received 5/23/2019, citing TelNet's estimated monthly recurring cost of approximately $1,076.50 before surcharges, burstable capacity from 36 to 50 talk paths, Troy headquarters and compatibility with the Mitel Connect system. Secondary computer lab upgrades total $103,619.00 from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund: $86,802.00 in monitors from Presidio via the MHEC contract and $16,817.00 in SSDs and RAM from Logical Ram Solutions, covering 721 22-inch monitors, 52 27-inch monitors and 335 SSD and RAM upgrades at Baker, Boulan, Larson, Smith, Athens, Troy High and TCCHS. The district will buy 1,250 iPads from Apple at $294 each for $367,500 via the REMC SPOT bid and 1,056 Rug-Ed cases at $22 each for $23,232, funded from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund and the Preschool Fund. Preschool laptops and desktops from Presidio total $39,823.00, including 26 Dell Latitude 3300 laptops at $621.00 each. First Student's transportation contract is extended three years from July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2022 with zero rate increases in 2019-2020 and 2020-2021 and 1.25% in 2021-2022, a $5,000 new-bus credit spread $2,000/$2,000/$1,000, and renegotiation if the 5-tier system converts to 3 or 4 tiers; the April 1, 2019 letter is from Area General Manager Douglas Meek. A tractor/loader goes to Rochester Lawn Equipment for $30,969.12 under MiDEAL contract 071B7700085.

**Personnel and closing.** Natalie Haezebrouck is recommended for a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure as Director of Teaching and Learning effective July 1, 2019. She began in Troy in 2005 as a 2nd grade teacher at Leonard and Schroeder Elementary Schools, became a Literacy Specialist at Leonard, and is a Curriculum and Instruction Specialist; she received the State of Michigan Elementary Literacy Teacher of the Year award in 2016 and holds degrees from Western Michigan University, Oakland University and Madonna University. Six applicants were interviewed (Joyce Brasington, Sarah Fairman, Megan Foster, Natalie Haezebrouck, Jeremy Whan, Stephanie Zendler) and three advanced. The meeting closed with Superintendent Dr. Rich Machesky introducing the "2018-2019 School Year in Review" video.
